questions.stem: The law of supply states that, other things being equal,

options.text: quantity supplied rises as price rises
quantity supplied falls as price rises
quantity supplied is unaffected by price
quantity supplied depends only on the cost of production

questions.explanation: A higher price raises the profit on each unit, so existing firms expand output and new firms enter. Price and quantity supplied therefore move together, giving an upward-sloping supply curve.

distractorRationale.b: That is the inverse relationship found in demand, not supply
distractorRationale.c: If price had no effect there would be no supply curve to draw
distractorRationale.d: Cost is an important determinant, but the law of supply is specifically about the good's own price

questions.stem: Which of the following distinguishes supply from stock?

options.text: Stock is offered for sale at a given price, while supply is held in the warehouse
Supply is the part of stock offered for sale at a given price in a given period
Supply and stock always have exactly the same value
Stock refers only to imported goods, while supply refers to local goods

questions.explanation: Stock is the total quantity in existence or held by sellers; supply is the portion actually placed on the market at a stated price and time. Hoarding is the clearest case of a large stock with a small supply.

distractorRationale.a: The two descriptions have been swapped
distractorRationale.c: They coincide only if a seller offers his entire stock at once, which is unusual
distractorRationale.d: Origin of the goods is irrelevant to the distinction

questions.stem: From the egg supply schedule — ₦1,000: 20 crates, ₦2,000: 35 crates, ₦3,000: 50 crates, ₦4,000: 62 crates, ₦5,000: 70 crates — how many extra crates are supplied when the price rises from ₦2,000 to ₦4,000? Give a number only.
questions.explanation: At ₦2,000 producers offer 35 crates and at ₦4,000 they offer 62 crates, so the extension of supply is 62 − 35 = 27 crates. The change came from the good's own price, so it is a movement along the supply curve.

questions.stem: A sharp rise in the price of poultry feed will most likely

options.text: shift the supply curve for eggs to the right
shift the supply curve for eggs to the left
cause a movement up along the supply curve for eggs
leave the supply of eggs completely unchanged

questions.explanation: Feed is an input, so its price is a cost of production, not the price of eggs. Higher costs make farmers willing to supply fewer crates at every price, which is a leftward shift of the whole supply curve.

distractorRationale.a: A rightward shift would follow a fall in costs or a subsidy
distractorRationale.c: Movements along the curve happen only when the price of eggs themselves changes
distractorRationale.d: Costs are a major determinant of supply, so supply must respond

questions.stem: Beef and hides are examples of goods in

options.text: competitive supply
joint supply
composite supply
derived supply

questions.explanation: Slaughtering one cow inevitably yields both beef and a hide, so producing more of one automatically produces more of the other. Crude oil and natural gas are related in the same way.

distractorRationale.a: Competitive supply applies where the same resources must be divided, such as maize versus cassava on one hectare
distractorRationale.c: Composite is a term used for demand, where one good serves several uses
distractorRationale.d: Derived demand exists, but there is no standard concept of derived supply in this context

questions.stem: Which of the following is an exception to the law of supply?

options.text: A rise in the price of cement leads cement factories to run extra shifts
A fish seller sells her entire catch cheaply at closing time rather than let it spoil
A subsidy on fertiliser leads farmers to produce more rice
New firms enter the noodle industry after prices rise

questions.explanation: With a highly perishable good the seller offers the same or more quantity even as the price falls, because unsold stock becomes worthless. The normal positive relationship between price and quantity supplied breaks down.

distractorRationale.a: This is the law of supply operating exactly as expected
distractorRationale.c: A subsidy shifts the supply curve rightward; it is a determinant of supply, not an exception to the law
distractorRationale.d: Entry of new firms in response to higher prices is part of the ordinary supply response

questions.stem: A government subsidy paid to producers increases the supply of a commodity.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. A subsidy lowers the effective cost of production, so producers are willing to offer more at every price and the supply curve shifts to the right. An excise tax has the opposite effect.

distractorRationale.b: This would only hold if the subsidy raised costs, which is the reverse of what a subsidy does

questions.stem: Traders withhold bags of cement from the market because they expect the price to rise next month. The immediate effect is that

options.text: supply decreases although total stock is unchanged
both supply and total stock decrease
supply increases because stock is being held
supply is unaffected because the price has not yet changed

questions.explanation: The cement still exists in the warehouses, so stock is the same, but less of it is being offered for sale today, so supply falls. This is precisely why hoarding pushes market prices up.

distractorRationale.b: Withholding goods does not destroy them, so total stock remains
distractorRationale.c: Holding stock back is the opposite of offering it for sale
distractorRationale.d: Expectations are an independent determinant of supply and act before the price actually changes
